name: Big Island Bees Beekeeping and Honey Tasting Tour

seo.metaTitle: Big Island Beekeeping Tour at Big Island Bees – Honest Review
seo.metaDescription: Compare the Big Island beekeeping tour at Big Island Bees: 1 hour, live hive demo, honey tasting, from $33 per adult, 48-hour cancellation. Read the pros and cons first.

cards.priceNote: adult (18+) on Greetwell, October 2026; a 2025 blog reported $30 adult / $20 youth / $10 child direct

overview.verdictSnippet: The Big Island Bees beekeeping tour in Captain Cook is a 1-hour farm visit with a live hive opened behind a screen, a short video and a tasting of single-flower honeys. It suits families and coffee-country day-trippers who want a cheap, low-effort stop. The main drawback is a weekday-only, two-slot schedule that must be reserved in advance.
highlights: A beekeeper opens a live hive while guests watch from behind a screened area; no bee suits are needed
Tasting of the farm's single-varietal honeys (lehua, macadamia blossom and a chili-pepper blend were named by a 2025 visitor)
Tours run Monday to Friday at 10:00 am and 1:00 pm only, with reservations required
Stroller and wheelchair accessible, with minimal walking and covered indoor and outdoor areas
Google listing shows 4.8 stars from 906 reviews as of October 2026
whatToExpect: You sign a liability waiver that is emailed the night before, then arrive at the farm on Meli Road in Captain Cook, about 35 minutes south of Kailua-Kona.
A 2025 visitor reported being greeted with iced tea and a honey-caramel-macadamia tart before the tour began.
The group watches a roughly 10-minute video on how honey goes from flower to jar, then asks the guide questions.
Outside, the guide puts on a bee suit and opens a working hive while you watch from behind a screen, learning about the queen and the colony.
The tour ends with a tasting of several honey varietals in the honey house.
Afterwards you can browse the farm store and the free museum, which does not need a reservation.
included: Guided hive tour and inspection
Short video on honey production
Samples of the farm's honey varietals
notIncluded: Honey jars, honey ice cream and other farm-store purchases
whatToBring: Comfortable clothes; the operator says shorts, sleeveless shirts and sandals are fine, but a 2025 visitor recommends closed-toe shoes because the grass is often wet
Sun protection and an umbrella, since rain is common on this part of the Kona coast
A pre-arranged ride back if you come by taxi or rideshare; the area is rural and cars are not readily available
restrictions: Reservations required; space is limited
Adult tickets are for ages 18+, youth tickets for ages 13 to 18; pricing for children under 13 was not shown on the fetched page
overview.cancellationPolicy: Cancel at least 48 hours before the tour for a full refund. Checked October 2026 on Greetwell.

location.meetingPoint: Big Island Bees, 82-1140 Meli Rd, Captain Cook, HI 96704

review.methodology: We read 1 Google review republished on Greetwell (September 2026), Greetwell's summary of its review feed, and 1 detailed blog review from a family visit (hawaiitravelwithkids.com, visited in February, year not stated). Public platform scores were collected in October 2026.

praise.title: Honey tasting with the story behind each varietal
praise.summary: Both reviews single out the tasting as the high point, because the guide explains the flower source and history of each honey rather than just handing out samples.
praise.example: — Google via Greetwell, 5★, September 2026: the sampling was much more enjoyable with story and history included

praise.title: Guide is knowledgeable and keeps it educational without being dull
praise.summary: The blog reviewer noted the guide had a zoology degree and more than six years of tour experience, and her 9-year-old asked questions throughout; the Google reviewer named the guide as the reason the tour worked.
praise.example: — Blog review, family visit in February: the hour felt educational but not boring, and the child stayed engaged for most of it

complaints.title: Younger children may lose interest before the hour is up
complaints.recency: most recent: year not stated (blog, February visit)
complaints.summary: The blog reviewer's 9-year-old drifted after about 45 minutes of the hive demonstration, and she doubted toddlers or preschoolers would last the full hour.
complaints.example: — Blog review, February: son lost interest after about 45 minutes at the hive

complaints.title: Wet grass and rain catch out guests in sandals and sundresses
complaints.recency: most recent: year not stated (blog, February visit)
complaints.summary: The operator says sandals are fine, but the blog reviewer saw other guests uncomfortable on wet grass and advises closed-toe shoes and an umbrella.
complaints.example: — Blog review, February: visitors in sundresses and sandals were uncomfortable on the wet grass

complaints.title: One report of a product-quality complaint
complaints.summary: Greetwell's summary of the review feed mentions a single complaint about product quality and notes the guide's comedy can feel heavy to some guests; we could not read the underlying review.

verdict.intro: At about $30 to $33 per adult for an hour, this is a reasonable add-on for anyone already driving the South Kona coffee and Captain Cook corridor, and the 4.8-star Google score across 906 reviews suggests the format works for most visitors. It is not a destination in itself: the weekday-only 10:00 am and 1:00 pm slots fill up, and there is no swimming, hiking or scenery component. Book it as a planned stop, not a spontaneous one.
bookIf: You are visiting Pu'uhonua o Honaunau, the Painted Church or a South Kona coffee farm on a weekday and want a second stop nearby
You travel with children aged roughly 8 and up who can sit through a 10-minute video and a 45-minute demonstration
You want to taste and buy single-source Hawaiian honeys with an explanation of each one
You need a wheelchair- or stroller-friendly activity with minimal walking
skipIf: Your only free days are Saturday or Sunday, when no tours run
You are traveling with toddlers or preschoolers who may not last the hour
You expect to handle bees or wear a suit; guests stay behind a screen throughout
You are staying at the Waikoloa resorts and would spend more than two hours round trip for a 1-hour stop
tips: Reserve online in advance; the operator and gohawaii.com both say tours fill up
Wear closed-toe shoes and bring an umbrella, as 1 of the 2 reviews we read describes wet grass and frequent rain
Arrange your return ride before arriving if you use a taxi or rideshare; Greetwell warns that cars are not readily available in the area
Allow time after the tour for the free museum and farm store, which are open weekdays 10:00 am to 3:00 pm
verdict.cta: Check live availability and prices on FareHarbor

faq.q: How long is the Big Island Bees beekeeping tour?
faq.a: The Big Island Bees beekeeping tour in Captain Cook lasts about 1 hour, with hawaii-guide.com quoting 1 to 1.5 hours. It combines a roughly 10-minute video, a live hive demonstration from behind a screen and a honey tasting, and you can stay longer afterwards for the free museum and farm store.

faq.q: What days and times does the Big Island Bees tour run?
faq.a: The beekeeping tour runs Monday through Friday only, at 10:00 am and 1:00 pm, according to gohawaii.com and hawaii-guide.com. The museum and store are open weekdays from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm. Reservations are required because space on each tour is limited, and the operator says slots fill up fast.

faq.q: How much does the Big Island Bees beekeeping tour cost?
faq.a: Greetwell listed the Big Island Bees tour at $33.21 per adult (18+), $22.14 per youth (13 to 18) and $27.68 for Hawaii residents with ID in October 2026. A family blog reported $30 adult, $20 youth and $10 child when booking direct in 2025, so check the live FareHarbor price before you go.

faq.q: Do you need protective clothing for the beekeeping tour?
faq.a: Protective clothing is not needed on the Big Island Bees tour because guests watch the open hive from behind a screened area while the beekeeper handles it. The operator says comfortable clothes, shorts and sandals are fine, though one blog reviewer recommends closed-toe shoes because the grass is often wet from rain.

faq.q: Is the Big Island Bees tour wheelchair and stroller accessible?
faq.a: Yes, the Big Island Bees beekeeping tour is listed as stroller and wheelchair accessible, with minimal walking and both indoor and outdoor areas under cover, according to the Greetwell listing. The hive demonstration and honey tasting take place in a small area near the farm store on Meli Road in Captain Cook.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for the Big Island Bees tour?
faq.a: The Big Island Bees beekeeping tour can be cancelled for a full refund if you give at least 48 hours' notice, according to the Greetwell listing checked in October 2026. The operator's own weather-cancellation terms were not shown on any page we fetched, so confirm them when you book.

name: Body Glove Deluxe Snorkel and Dolphin Watch Cruise, Kona

seo.metaTitle: Kona Snorkel Cruise with Body Glove – Real Reviews, Good and Bad
seo.metaDescription: Decide if the Body Glove Kona snorkel cruise is worth it: 4.5 hours, two meals, waterslide, from $150 per adult, dolphins not guaranteed. We read good and bad reviews.

cards.priceNote: adult sale price on Tripster; $173.43 on Greetwell and $180 plus tax on LoveBigIsland, October 2026

overview.verdictSnippet: Body Glove's Deluxe Snorkel and Dolphin Watch is a 4.5-hour Kona snorkel cruise on the 65-foot Kanoa II from Kailua Pier, with breakfast, BBQ lunch, a waterslide and about 2 hours at Red Hill. It suits families and first-time snorkelers who value amenities. The main drawback is that 3 of the 5 reviews we read found the reef itself underwhelming.
highlights: Departs Kailua Pier in downtown Kailua-Kona at 8:00 am and returns about 12:30 pm, every day
About 2 hours of snorkel time at the Red Hill marine sanctuary, with a 20-foot waterslide, high-dive platform, paddleboards and flotation mats off the boat
Breakfast (fruit, yogurt, granola, danishes) and a BBQ burger lunch are included; vegan taro burgers with 48 hours' notice
Wheelchair accessible via a custom ramp, with an accessible lower deck and restrooms; capacity up to 105 passengers
Dolphin sightings are not guaranteed; one 2019 reviewer was offered a free future trip after seeing none
whatToExpect: You check in 30 minutes before departure at Kailua Pier, sign a waiver and board the Kanoa II; the boat leaves on time and does not wait for latecomers.
Breakfast is served as the catamaran cruises north along the Kona coast, with the crew watching for spinner dolphins.
At Red Hill the boat anchors and the crew gives snorkel instruction and hands out masks, fins and flotation gear; you have roughly 2 hours in the water.
Between snorkel sessions you can use the 20-foot waterslide, the high-dive platform, paddleboards and the floating mat.
A BBQ burger lunch is served on deck, and the cash bar opens for cocktails and craft beer.
The boat returns to Kailua Pier at about 12:30 pm; there is no going ashore during the trip.
included: Continental breakfast and BBQ lunch (beef burger, chips, cookie; vegan taro burger with 48 hours' notice)
Soft drinks, juice and snacks
Snorkel mask, snorkel, fins, life vests and prescription masks (-1.5 to -7.0) at no charge
Snorkel instruction, flotation station, inner tubes, noodles, paddleboards and sea-view boards
Reef-safe sunscreen, ginger pills and ginger drink for seasickness
20-foot waterslide, high-dive platform, shade, restrooms and two freshwater showers
notIncluded: Cocktails, craft beer and spirits from the cash bar
Wetsuit rental ($10 on board, per Tripster)
Towels; LoveBigIsland notes they are not provided
Hotel pickup; taxis, Uber and Lyft are the suggested options
whatToBring: Swimsuit, towel and sunglasses
Cash or a card for the bar and retail items
Your own snorkel gear if you prefer it; full-face masks are not permitted
A handicapped parking placard if you need accessible pier parking, requested at booking
restrictions: Full-face snorkel masks are not allowed
Children of all ages may join, but must be accompanied by an adult 18 or over
Liability waiver signed at check-in; no smoking on the vessel
Dolphin and whale sightings are not guaranteed
No refunds for late arrival or motion sickness
overview.cancellationPolicy: Full refund if you cancel at least 48 hours ahead for parties of 9 or fewer, 72 hours for parties of 10 to 19, and 7 days for parties of 20 or more; full refund if the operator cancels. Checked October 2026 on Greetwell. Note that the VELTRA (hawaiiactivities.com) listing applies stricter 3-, 4- and 8-business-day windows for its own bookings.

location.meetingPoint: Kailua Pier, north end of Ali'i Drive, downtown Kailua-Kona, in front of the Courtyard King Kamehameha's Kona Beach Hotel
location.checkIn: 30 minutes before departure (about 7:30 am for the 8:00 am cruise)
location.parking: Free parking at the Body Glove office, 75-5629 Kuakini Hwy, one block from the pier; paid parking at the Courtyard King Kamehameha hotel; accessible pier parking is very limited

review.methodology: We read 5 individual reviews: 3 on Tripster (October 2015 to June 2019), 1 on VELTRA/hawaiiactivities.com (September 2025) and 1 Google review republished on Greetwell (September 2026). Star ratings were shown for only 2 of them. Platform scores were collected in October 2026.

praise.title: Friendly, helpful crew
praise.summary: Even the two reviewers who were disappointed by the snorkeling praised the crew, and the two most recent reviews call the staff the best part of the trip.
praise.example: — Google via Greetwell, 5★, September 2026: the crew and the ship are exceptional

praise.title: Well-equipped boat with toys and flotation
praise.summary: Reviewers mention the paddleboards, the large floating mat and the quality of the snorkel equipment, which is relevant for groups with non-swimmers.
praise.example: — VELTRA, September 2025: staff, boat and equipment were excellent, and it was fun for a first-time snorkeler

praise.title: Plentiful food
praise.summary: Both older Tripster reviewers called the lunch tasty and generous and the breakfast adequate.
praise.example: — Tripster, June 2019: the continental breakfast was fine and the lunch was tasty and plentiful

complaints.title: Snorkel site at Red Hill is less rewarding than shore snorkeling
complaints.summary: Three Tripster reviewers said they saw more fish from shore and that the reef had less variety than expected; one had expected Kealakekua Bay, which this cruise does not visit.
complaints.example: — Tripster, October 2015: one of the weakest snorkel spots in seven trips to the Big Island
complaints.operatorResponse: One reviewer in June 2019 was told they could book a future tour free because no dolphins were seen.

complaints.title: Expectations about dolphins are not met
complaints.summary: One reviewer saw no dolphins at all; another expected to swim with them and only watched a sleeping pod from the boat. The operator states sightings are not guaranteed and there is no in-water dolphin encounter.
complaints.example: — Tripster, October 2015: do not expect to swim with the dolphins

complaints.title: Waiting around when add-ons are booked
complaints.summary: A reviewer who booked a Snuba add-on had to wait for a second group and missed part of lunch service; this is a single, dated report.
complaints.example: — Tripster, October 2015: booked Snuba but had to wait for a second group while food was served

review.operatorWide: Body Glove Hawaii's listings across platforms score 4.5 to 4.8 with thousands of reviews, and the same Kanoa II vessel runs the operator's Historical Lunch Cruise in the afternoon.

verdict.intro: At $150 to $180 per adult, this Kona snorkel cruise is worth it for families and nervous snorkelers who will use the waterslide, flotation gear and included meals, and the 4.5 to 4.8 ratings across more than 8,000 reviews show most passengers leave satisfied. Experienced snorkelers chasing the best reef should look at a Kealakekua Bay trip instead; 3 of the 5 reviews we read rated Red Hill below a good shore snorkel. Treat dolphins as a bonus, not the reason to book.
bookIf: You are traveling with children, non-swimmers or first-time snorkelers who need flotation gear and a calm, amenity-heavy boat
You want breakfast and lunch included so a morning on the water covers a full meal
You or a companion uses a wheelchair; the ramp and lower deck are built for it
You are staying in Kailua-Kona or Keauhou, within 45 minutes of Kailua Pier
skipIf: You have already snorkeled from shore at Kahalu'u or Two Step and want a clearly better reef
You expect to swim with dolphins; this is watching from the boat only
You get seasick easily; there are no refunds for motion sickness
You are staying in Hilo or Volcano and face a 3-hour drive each way for a morning trip
tips: Park free at the Body Glove office on Kuakini Hwy, one block from the pier, rather than paying at the hotel lot
Order vegan, vegetarian or gluten-free meals at least 48 hours ahead by phone
Bring your own towel; LoveBigIsland notes they are not provided
Sit on the lower deck if you are prone to seasickness, and take the free ginger before departure
Compare prices: in October 2026 Tripster showed $149.99, Greetwell $173.43 and LoveBigIsland $180 plus tax for the same adult ticket

faq.q: Where does the Body Glove Kona snorkel cruise depart from?
faq.a: The Body Glove Deluxe Snorkel and Dolphin Watch departs from Kailua Pier at the north end of Ali'i Drive in downtown Kailua-Kona, in front of the Courtyard King Kamehameha's Kona Beach Hotel. Boarding starts 30 minutes before the 8:00 am departure, and free parking is available at the Body Glove office one block away on Kuakini Highway.

faq.q: How long is the Body Glove snorkel and dolphin watch cruise?
faq.a: The Body Glove snorkel and dolphin watch cruise lasts about 4.5 hours, leaving Kailua Pier at 8:00 am and returning around 12:30 pm. Roughly 2 of those hours are spent snorkeling and using the waterslide at the Red Hill marine sanctuary, with breakfast on the way out and BBQ lunch on board.

faq.q: Are dolphins guaranteed on the Body Glove cruise?
faq.a: Dolphins are not guaranteed on the Body Glove Deluxe Snorkel and Dolphin Watch, and the operator states this on every listing we checked. Spinner dolphins are watched from the boat only, with no in-water encounter. One June 2019 reviewer who saw none was offered a free future trip, but that offer is not a published policy.

faq.q: What food is included on the Body Glove Deluxe Snorkel cruise?
faq.a: The Body Glove Deluxe Snorkel cruise includes a continental breakfast of fruit, yogurt, granola and danishes, then a BBQ lunch of a beef burger with chips and a cookie, plus soft drinks, juice and snacks. Vegan taro burgers and gluten-free or vegetarian meals are available at no charge with at least 48 hours' notice.

faq.q: Is the Body Glove Kona snorkel cruise wheelchair accessible?
faq.a: Yes, the Body Glove Kona snorkel cruise on the Kanoa II is wheelchair accessible through a customized ramp that fits manual and electric wheelchairs and scooters, and the lower deck including restrooms is fully accessible. Accessible parking at Kailua Pier is very limited and first-come, so request a pass at booking and bring your placard.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for the Body Glove snorkel cruise?
faq.a: The Body Glove snorkel cruise refunds in full with 48 hours' notice for groups of 9 or fewer, 72 hours for 10 to 19 people and 7 days for 20 or more, according to Greetwell in October 2026. Bookings through VELTRA use longer 3-, 4- and 8-business-day windows. There is no refund for late arrival or seasickness.

faq.q: Can you use a full-face snorkel mask on the Body Glove cruise?
faq.a: Full-face snorkel masks are not permitted on the Body Glove Deluxe Snorkel and Dolphin Watch cruise. The crew provides standard masks, snorkels and fins, including prescription masks from -1.5 to -7.0 at no extra charge, and you are welcome to bring your own conventional snorkel gear instead.

seo.metaDescription: Review the Kohala Divers two-site Kohala Coast dive charter from Kawaihae: 6 hours, two reef dives or guided snorkel, from $229, 48-hour cancellation. See pros and cons.

cards.priceNote: certified diver, before taxes and fees; guided snorkeler $189

overview.verdictSnippet: The Kohala Divers two-site Kohala Coast dive charter is a 6-hour morning boat trip from Kawaihae that takes certified divers and guided snorkelers to two reef sites between Puako and Kohala. It suits mixed groups staying at the Kohala resorts; the drawback is the $229-plus price and a strict 48-hour cancellation window.
highlights: Departs Kawaihae Harbor at 7:30 am and visits two reef sites chosen by the captain on the day
Divers and snorkelers share the same boat; snorkelers get their own guide and pay $189 before tax
46-foot boat Namaka with shade, two heated freshwater showers, a marine toilet and a camera rinse tank
Dive groups are capped at 6 per instructor; the boat carries up to 18 divers
Complimentary shuttle from several Kohala Coast resorts according to the Love Big Island listing
whatToExpect: You check in at the Kohala Divers shop in the Kawaihae Shopping Center, 61-3665 Akoni Pule Hwy, and show your certification card.
The boat leaves Kawaihae Harbor around 7:30 am and heads south toward the Puako and Kohala reefs.
The captain picks the two sites after departure based on sea conditions; both 2022 and 2024 Undercurrent reports describe bottom times of about an hour.
Divers descend in groups of up to 6 with a guide; snorkelers stay above the same reef with their own guide.
Between dives the crew serves snacks and drinks, and there is a surface interval on board.
The second site often includes arches and swim-throughs; the 2024 Undercurrent reviewer saw turtles and an octopus but no sharks or mantas.
The boat returns to Kawaihae by early afternoon, about 6 hours after departure.

review.methodology: We read 3 individual reviews for this charter in October 2026: 1 on Greetwell (July 2026, 5 stars) and 2 detailed diver reports on Undercurrent (June 2022 and September 2024, both rating the dive operation 5 of 5). No 1–2 star reviews were found, so the complaints below come from critical remarks inside positive reports.

praise.title: Crew is organized and hands-on with gear and boarding
praise.summary: All three reviewers praise the crew for helping with tanks, in-water assistance and getting back aboard, and one describes the operation as well organized over five separate trips.
praise.example: — Undercurrent, dive operation 5/5, September 2024: the crew helped with tanks and re-boarding, and guides knew each site and pointed out unusual species.

praise.title: Good handling of cameras and a relaxed pace for photographers
praise.summary: Both Undercurrent reports rate photography conditions 4 of 5 and say guides let divers linger to shoot, with the crew careful when passing cameras.
praise.example: — Undercurrent, 5/5 service, June 2022: "The crew does an excellent job of handling and care of cameras."

complaints.title: Few large animals; reef life is mostly turtles and small fish
complaints.summary: Both Undercurrent reviewers rated large fish and pelagics 1 of 5 and corals 3 of 5; sightings were turtles, an octopus and at most one or two sharks or dolphins across multiple dives.
complaints.example: — Undercurrent, September 2024: frequent turtles, but no sharks, mantas, dolphins or whales recorded across the trip.

review.operatorWide: The 2024 Undercurrent reviewer also took a PADI Advanced Open Water course with Kohala Divers and was satisfied with the instructor; the 2022 reviewer noted private guides had become expensive.

verdict.intro: At $229 per diver before tax, this charter is worth it for certified divers staying between Waikoloa and Kawaihae who want a short drive and a mixed-ability boat; the Kona dive shops are 45 minutes further south. Expect healthy coral, arches and turtles rather than mantas or sharks, which the two Undercurrent reports confirm are rare here. Book elsewhere if you want a specific site, because the captain chooses both on the day.

faq.q: Can you kayak to the Captain Cook Monument on your own?
faq.a: You cannot land a self-guided rental kayak at the Captain Cook Monument; only permitted guided tours such as the Kona Boys Morning Magic trip may land at Kaʻawaloa. Without a guided kayak, the alternatives are the steep Kaʻawaloa trail on foot or a licensed snorkel boat that stays offshore.

faq.q: How long is the paddle across Kealakekua Bay?

faq.q: What is included in the Kona Boys kayak and snorkel tour?

faq.a: On the Kona Honu Divers blackwater dive you stay between the surface and about 60 feet, held to the boat by a main line with a 12–15-foot personal tether clipped to your BCD. The ocean beneath is more than 4,000 feet deep, which is why buoyancy control and a BCD with a bladder are required.

faq.q: What animals do you see on a Kona blackwater dive?
faq.a: Reviewers of the Kona Honu Divers blackwater dive report jellies and gelatinous animals, larval fish with bioluminescent colors, squid, and in March 2020 three pods of dolphins feeding near the surface. faq.q: How much is the Kona Honu Divers Open Water course?

faq.q: How many days does the Open Water course take?
faq.a: The operator schedules 3 days of in-person training after a self-paced eLearning day of 8 to 12 hours: about 7 hours of confined water, then two days of 2 open-water dives each, roughly 5 hours apiece. faq.q: Where are the open-water dives?
faq.a: Dives 1 and 2 are made from shore or boat and dives 3 and 4 from the Honu One, the operator's 46-foot custom dive boat, on the Kona coast. The operator's hawaii.com listing adds that snacks and water are provided on board. Exact sites depend on conditions on the day.

faq.q: What are the prerequisites?

faq.q: Is the class size small?

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for courses?

Arriving more than 15 minutes late or not showing up forfeits the fee. If the operator cancels for weather or safety, you are rescheduled or refunded in full.
